```json
{
  "winner": "B",
  "reasons": [
    "B's demand evidence points at the solution itself. The Reddit threads (2022–2025) describe crawlers receiving empty HTML shells, and developers in them ask for prerendering by name. A's quotes describe general decision paralysis and never ask for a research or trade-off tool.",
    "B's willingness to pay rests on usage-tiered recurring pricing ($49/$149/$349 per month), a vendor operating since 2014, and a named paying customer, though that customer comes from a vendor testimonial. A's price anchors come from competitors, and at least one of them (Insightloop) is pre-launch.",
    "B's revenue model is recurring, infrastructure-like usage with low churn pressure once installed. A's own brief flags that 'big decision' usage is episodic, and that a ~$104 cost per lead sits badly against a ~$60 one-off price.",
    "A carries a product-premise risk that B does not. A category vendor (Gixo) admits a human must verify every number and recommendation, and the brief raises unrebutted substitution risk from general-purpose LLM chat. B's core value, serving rendered HTML to bots, is deterministic and verifiable.",
    "Both markets are crowded. B's crowding reflects a mature, proven-paying category in which a solo builder can compete on price or niche, for example AI-crawler visibility. A's crowding reflects many near-identical new entrants with better data infrastructure and no demonstrated wedge.",
    "B's main threat is Google's 2022 downgrade of dynamic rendering. That is a long-term market-shrinkage risk, and it matters less for a 90-day first-customer goal than A's immediate unit-economics and differentiation problems."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "Idea A's demand evidence consists of two social posts about the difficulty of choosing between reasonable options, and neither expresses a desire to pay for a tool. The LinkedIn quote ('the spreadsheet can't choose between them. Only you can.') argues against the premise that an automated tool delivers the decision.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate confidence. Both briefs show saturated markets, and B has real weaknesses. Its Reddit quotes are cited by subreddit and year without URLs. Its named customer comes from a vendor testimonial. Its only cheap acquisition channel (community engagement) is unsourced, and the sourced SEO CAC of $480–942 with a 7-month payback is slow for a 90-day window. B wins mainly because its demand and pay signals are specific to the product, while A's are generic and partly self-undermining."
}
```
